blocks.prompt: 10. If \(z = x + iy\) and \(\arg\left(\frac{\overline{z} - 1 + 2i}{\overline{z} + 1 - 2i}\right) = \frac{9\pi}{4}\), show that \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 2y - 5 = 0\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh 'show that' (saabit karein) wala locus ka sawal hai, jis mein ek fraction ka argument diya hai. Pehli baat: \(\frac{9\pi}{4}\) dekh kar ghabrayein nahi; yeh \(2\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}\) hai, yani ek poora chakkar aur \(\frac{\pi}{4}\). Is liye fraction ki direction \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) hai, jahan real part aur imaginary part barabar hote hain. Plan: upar aur neeche ko a + ib mein likhein, neeche ke conjugate se zarb kar ke neeche ko real banayein, phir real part = imaginary part rakh dein.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = x + iy\) aur \(\arg\left(\frac{\overline{z} - 1 + 2i}{\overline{z} + 1 - 2i}\right) = \frac{9\pi}{4}\).
To prove (saabit karna hai): \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 2y - 5 = 0\).
Method (tareeqa): agar \(\arg w = \frac{\pi}{4}\) ho aur \(w = a + ib\), to \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{b}{a} = 1\), yani \(a = b\) (aur dono positive).

Qadam 1: \(\frac{9\pi}{4}\) ka matlab kya hai?
\[\dfrac{9\pi}{4} = 2\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
Kyun: \(2\pi\) ek poora chakkar hai jo hamein wapas usi direction par le aata hai, jaise ghari ki sui 12 ghante baad wahin aa jaati hai. Is liye fraction \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) ki direction (first quadrant) mein hai. Note: \(\frac{9\pi}{4}\) principal value nahi; is ki principal value \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) hai.

Qadam 2: Upar aur neeche ko a + ib form mein likhein
\[\overline{z} = x - iy\]
\[\text{Top} = (x - 1) + (2 - y)i\]
\[\text{Bottom} = (x + 1) - (y + 2)i\]
Kyun: \(\overline{z} = x - iy\) rakha, phir real aur imaginary hisse alag ikatthe kiye. Upar: \(x - iy - 1 + 2i\); neeche: \(x - iy + 1 - 2i\).
Dhyan dein: neeche ka imaginary part \(-y - 2 = -(y + 2)\) hai; minus ko bahar nikaalte waqt dono terms ka sign badalta hai.

Qadam 3: Neeche ke conjugate se zarb karein
Neeche ka conjugate: \((x + 1) + (y + 2)i\).
Naya neeche: \((x + 1)^{2} + (y + 2)^{2}\), jo ek positive real number hai.
Kyun: kisi number ko us ke conjugate se zarb karein to \(a^{2} + b^{2}\) milta hai, jis mein i nahi hota. Is ke baad fraction = (naya upar)/(positive number), aur positive number se taqseem direction nahi badalta. Is liye ab sirf naye upar ki direction dekhni hai.

Qadam 4: Naye upar ka real part
\((a + bi)(c + di)\) ka real part \(= ac - bd\) hota hai, jahan \(a = x - 1\), \(b = 2 - y\), \(c = x + 1\), \(d = y + 2\).
\[\text{Re} = (x - 1)(x + 1) - (2 - y)(2 + y)\]
\[= x^{2} - 1 - (4 - y^{2})\]
\[= x^{2} + y^{2} - 5\]
Kyun: \((x-1)(x+1)\) aur \((2-y)(2+y)\) dono 'difference of squares' (\((p - q)(p + q) = p^{2} - q^{2}\)) hain. Real part mein \(-bd\) is liye aata hai ke \(bi \cdot di = bd\,i^{2} = -bd\).

Qadam 5: Naye upar ka imaginary part
Imaginary part \(= ad + bc\):
\[\text{Im} = (x - 1)(y + 2) + (2 - y)(x + 1)\]
\[= xy + 2x - y - 2\]
\[\quad + 2x + 2 - xy - y\]
\[= 4x - 2y\]
Kyun: dono brackets khole; \(xy\) aur \(-xy\) cancel ho gaye, aur \(-2\), \(+2\) bhi cancel ho gaye.
Dhyan dein: bracket kholte waqt har term ko har term se zarb karein (chaar products); ek term chhoot jaana aam ghalti hai.

Qadam 6: Real part = imaginary part rakhein
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 5 = 4x - 2y\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 2y - 5 = 0\]
Kyun: direction \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) ka matlab \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\text{Im}}{\text{Re}} = 1\), yani Re = Im. Phir sab terms ek taraf le aaye. (Bilkul sahi baat yeh hai ke points ke liye \(4x - 2y > 0\) bhi chahiye, is liye locus is circle ka ek hissa (arc) hai.)

Tasdeeq (check): \(x = 5, y = 0\) circle par hai (\(25 - 20 - 5 = 0\)). Is ke liye \(\overline{z} = 5\):
\[\dfrac{5 - 1 + 2i}{5 + 1 - 2i} = \dfrac{4 + 2i}{6 - 2i}\]
\[= \dfrac{(4 + 2i)(6 + 2i)}{40} = \dfrac{20 + 20i}{40}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}i\]
Real part = imaginary part > 0, is liye argument \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) hai (\(\frac{9\pi}{4}\) wali direction). Sahi.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 2y - 5 = 0\). Yeh ek circle ki equation hai (centre \((2, -1)\), radius \(\sqrt{10}\)).
